title: Regressoscope: slice-mapper and unified p95/p99 dashboards (route/model/region)
creator: Marcos Rivera
description:
Problem: We currently lack a single operational surface that ties p95/p99 latency signals to request provenance (route, model, region) plus the upstream tokens/sec load narratives used to reproduce regressions. Engineers waste time stitching traces, synthetic runs, and dashboards during incidents.

Goal: Deliver a slice-centric observability dashboard ("Regressoscope") that: 1) surfaces p95 and p99 trends by route/model/region, 2) links each latency slice to the tokens/sec load profile and representative synthetic playback, 3) exposes baseline anchors and automatically detects regressions using a configurable statistical guardrail, and 4) supports alerting and rollout gating for canary/deployment workflows.

High-level approach:
- Ingest percentile telemetry emitted by the runtime (per-request route + model + region tags) and compute rolling p95/p99 rollups with multiple windows (1m, 5m, 1h).
- Correlate latency rollups with tokens/sec histograms from the load harness and the production TPS stream.
- Implement a slice-mapper service that maps an anomalous percentile bucket to a small set of representative request traces and a synthetic replay recipe (playback seed + profile).
- Build a multi-pane dashboard: Overview (global heatmap), Route view, Model view, Region view, and Replay panel.
- Add a regression detector that evaluates current percentile against baseline anchors using a robust non-parametric test and marks regressions with confidence scores.
- Integrate with alerting and rollout APIs to support canary blocking rules and automatic fallback for severe regressions.

Out of scope for this ticket: deep APM-level stack traces and request body scrubbing (handled by other privacy tasks).

Operational acceptance will require a migration doc and a short playbook for on-call engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: New Regressoscope dashboard deployed with Overview, Route, Model and Region tabs visible to Console users with observability role.
Telemetry: p95 and p99 rollups computed and stored for 1m/5m/1h windows with tags: route, model, region and shown in dashboard panels.
Correlation: Each latency slice row links to a tokens/sec time series and to the most-likely synthetic replay recipe generated by the load harness.

Regression detector: Baseline anchors can be created and a non-parametric regression detector flags regressions with >=80% confidence; alerts are emitted to the test Slack channel and can be used as a canary gate.
Bench integration: Tokens/sec playback from Loadsmith (or equivalent) can be launched from the dashboard and returns a job id and link to the bench run.
Perf tests: End-to-end load tests show dashboard signals move within expected bounds; synthetic replay reproduces observed tail increases in at least 3 out of 5 validation runs.
Docs: On-call playbook and migration notes published and linked from the dashboard header.
Privacy/Security: Telemetry contains no plaintext request bodies; audit log entries exist for dashboard access and playback initiation.
